fields.summary: Fix upload limit blocking buyers on their first upload
fields.description_markdown:
## Case

Some buyers hit the upload limit on their very first image upload, even though they have not uploaded anything before. Reported by seller Lyot.

Root cause (confirmed by dev): the upload limit is counted per visitor + product + 1 hour. A visitor is normally identified by a random visitor ID (thumbmark) fetched from the server and stored in the browser. When the visitor ID has not been fetched yet at upload time, TIB falls back to an ID generated from device info (phone model, screen size, language, timezone, OS version). This fallback ID collides across devices: two different buyers on the same device model and region get the same ID, so unrelated buyers share the same hourly upload quota and one of them gets blocked on the first upload.

Workaround: the seller already fetches the visitor ID before the buyer uploads, but this does not fully solve it, especially in private/incognito browsers where the ID may not be stored.

![](blob:<attachment image, media id b9079258-5671-4d81-ab14-4060c80f1c59, not downloaded>)

## Solution

Remove the device-info-based fallback ID and generate a random ID per browser instead, so different visitors never share the same quota.

Fetching the visitor ID earlier only reduces the chance of falling back (network loss, timeout, incognito); it does not eliminate the collision on its own.

```
instance: https://admin.teeinblue.com/admin/instances/6717
```

_Issue created in Slack from a_ [message](https://ownego.slack.com/archives/C0A8G9G622Z/p1789615646209449?thread_ts=1789615646.209449&cid=C0A8G9G622Z)_._

comments.body_markdown:
## Background

To enforce the hourly upload limit, the SDK sends a "thumbmark" (visitor ID) with every upload so the backend knows which visitor's quota to count against. Normally this thumbmark is fetched from the server. If that fetch fails or is too slow, the SDK falls back to generating its own ID client-side from browser/device info instead — and that fallback is where this bug lives.

## What changed

The bug: when a customer's browser hadn't yet fetched its signed visitor ID at upload time, the SDK fell back to an ID built from device info (phone model, screen size, language, timezone). Different customers on the same device model got the _same_ fallback ID and ended up sharing one hourly upload quota — so the second person got blocked on their very first upload.

Fix has three parts now:

1. The fallback ID is random and unique per browser (not derived from device info anymore), so it can no longer collide between different customers.
2. The SDK fetches the visitor ID as soon as the page loads instead of waiting until the first upload — so in most cases the fallback path won't even be needed.
3. The fetch itself is now more resilient: longer timeout (3s → 8s, safe since it's a background page-load fetch, not something blocking the upload button) and one retry on a network error/5xx before giving up (not on a 429, retrying into a rate limit can't help).

## Before you start

* Rate limiting only applies to uploads that use an AI effect (Remove Background, AI Enhance/Image Filter, Text-to-Image, etc.). A plain upload with no effect is never limited, so pick a product/campaign field that has one of these effects turned on.
* Test on **staging** — the throttle window there is 5 minutes instead of 1 hour in production, so you don't have to wait as long between checks.
* Default limit: 5 uploads per window per visitor.
* **Important for step 3 below:** the signed thumbmark is cached in `localStorage` (key `teeinblue_signed_thumbmark`) with no expiry once successfully fetched. If you already tested this on staging before, that key is likely still set in your browser, and you will NOT see a new `GET /thumbmark` request on reload — that's the cache working correctly, not a bug. Clear it (DevTools → Application → Local Storage → remove `teeinblue_signed_thumbmark`) or use a fresh Incognito window before checking step 3.

## Test steps

**1. Force the bug's exact scenario (the collision check — this is the main thing to verify)**

* Open Chrome DevTools → Network tab → **Request blocking** → block the URL pattern `*/merchant/*/thumbmark*`. This makes the SDK unable to get a real visitor ID, forcing it onto the fallback path every time — the same situation the reported customers hit.
* Open **two separate Incognito/Private windows** (same browser/device, simulating "different customers on the same device model").
* In Window A, upload one image (with the AI effect) on the test product → should succeed.
* In Window B, upload one image within the same window → **Expected: also succeeds.** ❌ If you see "Upload limit exceeded" here on the very first attempt, the bug is back.

**2. Confirm real rate limiting still works (regression check)**

* Still with the thumbmark endpoint blocked, in one window keep uploading in the same session until you hit the limit (5th upload).
* The 6th upload should still correctly show "Upload limit exceeded" — confirms a genuine repeat visitor is still limited, not accidentally exempted by the fix.
* Reload the page and try uploading once more (still same 5-min window) → should still be blocked. This confirms the fallback ID stays consistent for the same visitor across page reloads instead of resetting.

**3. Confirm the "fetch earlier" improvement**

* Unblock the thumbmark URL. Make sure `localStorage` is clear for this domain (see note above), or use a fresh Incognito window.
* Open Network tab, reload the page.
* You should see a request to `/merchant/{platform}/thumbmark` fire immediately on page load, before touching any upload field.
* Then upload an image and confirm **no second** request to that endpoint fires — it reuses the one from page load.

**4. Sanity check normal flow**

* With nothing blocked, do a few normal uploads (with and without AI effects) — should behave exactly as before, no new errors.

## Known follow-up (separate from this PR)

The thumbmark-issuance endpoint's own rate limit is keyed by IP only (not per-shop), so customers behind a shared/CGNAT IP (e.g. mobile carriers) could still occasionally hit it and fall back. We may raise that limit in a follow-up `teeinblue-api` PR — will track separately if needed.

fields.summary: Enhance security for public merchant routes and bypassable rate limits

facts_carried_forward.fact: GET merchant/{platform}/thumbmark was introduced by TIB-5341. It issues a server-signed identity of the form {id}.{signature} and is itself throttled 30/min per IP.
ValidateThumbmark verifies the signature but ALSO accepts the legacy unsigned format during a soft-transition window, logged via thumbmark.validation.legacy_format_used.

AI-effect routes (photo-upload, photo-base64-upload, apply-effects, image-filter-effects(/async), customer-uploads/generate, generate-from-multiple-images) carry an IP backstop of 50/hour IN ADDITION to the existing per-thumbmark limit.
The per-thumbmark limit on AI generation is default 5/hour; exceeding it returns 429 with rateLimitExceeded: true.
The SDK ThumbmarkService fetch had a 3s timeout and fell back to the old local browser fingerprint on failure/timeout. This is exactly the fallback TIB-5460 replaces.
A tampered signature must return 401. Legacy raw 32-char alphanumeric X-Thumbmark-ID must still succeed (not 401) during the transition window.
Laravel default throttle keys on domain+IP only, which caused all throttled routes to share one bucket; TIB-5341 gave each route an independent bucket.

TIB-5341 explicitly scoped itself 'server-side only - no API client (SDK) changes required' in Constraints, yet its own implementation comment did change teeinblue-sdk ThumbmarkService. The SDK-side fallback that TIB-5460 now fixes therefore arrived through a change that the issue's own constraints said would not happen.
